title: Twilight Zone (pinball)
creator: Pat Lawlor (lead designer)
description: Bally/Midway widebody-era WPC pinball machine released in April 1993, designed by Pat Lawlor with Larry DeMar and Ted Estes after Lawlor was given full creative control following The Addams Family. It took about 16 months to design and shipped with more features and patents than any earlier pinball; 15,235 units were built. Signature toys include a working gumball machine that stores three balls, a lighter white ceramic Powerball that ignores magnets, a working 12-hour clock, the magnet-flipper Powerfield mini-playfield, and slot machine, player piano and camera targets.
tz_connection: Licensed adaptation of the original series: the playfield and backbox reference dozens of episodes and Tim Kitzrow voices a Rod Serling-style narrator.
recommendation_reason: The single most celebrated Twilight Zone game and a landmark of pinball design.

title: The Twilight Zone
creator: Covenant Technologies (developer)
publisher: First Row Software Publishing, Inc. (King of Prussia, PA)
description: Parser-driven text-and-graphics adventure released in 1988 for Amiga and IBM PC/DOS, licensed from CBS. The manual bills it as the first of a planned series, with the subtitle 'The Crossroads of Imagination', and credits concept to Dr. Michael M. Breggar, Terrence R. Boyle and Steven Trippe, graphics to Patrick Moran and programming to A. Caleb Gattegno. It was not copy protected and offered UNDO/OOPS commands, five save slots and a 200-point score.
tz_connection: Officially licensed (copyright 1988 CBS Inc.) adventure built like a standalone Twilight Zone episode.
recommendation_reason: The first licensed Twilight Zone computer game, with a manual scan available.

title: The Twilight Zone Game
description: Ideal's 1964 tie-in board game for 2 to 4 players. Pawns start at the center and race along a maze-like 'Road to Reality' toward their home corners, steered by a three-ring spinner that sets movement, allows blocking cards to be played, or forces a player onto a rival's path. 'Hand of Destiny' spaces dictate a player's next direction. It shipped with a board, four colored pawns, 12 blocking cards and a spinner, with the rules printed inside the box lid. No designer is credited.
tz_connection: Officially licensed board game released in the original series' final year.
recommendation_reason: The only board game released during the original run.

title: Proposed Twilight Zone board game (Boyd Specialty Company, 1958)
creator: John J. Boyd, Sr.
description: In 1958, before the pilot was made, Boyd Specialty Company president John J. Boyd, Sr. wrote to Rod Serling asking to license the show's name for a board game and to place it in episodes as an advertising tie-in, promising it would beat Monopoly. Serling said the show was too early for merchandise and referred him to CBS programming head William Dozier. The game was never made.
tz_connection: The earliest known merchandise pitch for The Twilight Zone, preserved in Serling's correspondence.
recommendation_reason: A charming documented prehistory of Twilight Zone games.
